summary:
TerraField Atlas is an Earth-observation and agricultural intelligence platform designed to help farmers, agronomists, and agricultural researchers make more informed crop-rotation decisions using NASA data. Our project combines satellite-derived environmental indicators, meteorological observations, soil information, and crop characteristics to investigate changing agricultural conditions and evaluate crop-rotation strategies.

The platform focuses on translating complex Earth-observation data into accessible, location-based insights. Users can explore environmental conditions, examine historical trends, identify potential anomalies, and compare agricultural planning scenarios with transparent explanations of the underlying evidence and its limitations.

Addressing NASA's Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data challenge, TerraField Atlas demonstrates how space-based observations can support more resilient agricultural planning. Its broader vision incorporates environmental trend analysis and satellite-based fire monitoring to strengthen landscape intelligence.

We believe accessible Earth science can help communities better understand environmental change, improve agricultural decision-making, and build resilience against climate variability.
details:
TerraField Atlas

NASA Earth Intelligence for Agricultural Resilience

What does it do and how does it work?

TerraField Atlas is a geospatial agricultural intelligence platform that transforms Earth-observation data into actionable insights for more resilient agricultural planning. It addresses NASA's Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data challenge by connecting satellite-derived environmental observations, climate indicators, soil characteristics and crop requirements to support informed crop-rotation decisions.

The platform is designed around an integrated workflow. Users select or define an agricultural area, examine relevant environmental indicators, explore historical changes and evaluate alternative crop-rotation scenarios. Its analytical engine considers factors such as precipitation patterns, temperature, vegetation conditions, soil moisture, soil properties, crop water requirements and planting periods.

Rather than simply displaying satellite imagery, TerraField Atlas aims to translate observations into understandable agricultural intelligence. Users can compare environmental trends, examine possible anomalies, assess the suitability of different crop sequences and understand the evidence, assumptions and limitations behind each assessment.

What benefits does it provide?

The platform makes complex Earth-observation information more accessible to people who need it for agricultural planning. Its benefits include:

  • Evidence-based agricultural planning: Helps farmers and agricultural advisors consider environmental conditions when evaluating crop-rotation options.
  • Environmental awareness: Makes historical changes in rainfall, temperature, vegetation and soil moisture easier to investigate.
  • Soil-health considerations: Incorporates soil characteristics and crop compatibility into rotation assessments.
  • Climate resilience: Helps users explore agricultural strategies under changing environmental conditions.
  • Explainable intelligence: Makes the evidence and assumptions behind recommendations visible instead of relying on unexplained AI-generated suggestions.
  • Scalable geospatial analysis: Establishes a foundation that can support agricultural communities, research institutions and environmental organisations across different regions.

What is the intended impact?

Our initial focus is Uganda and the wider East African agricultural landscape, where access to understandable environmental information can support farmers, cooperatives, researchers and agricultural extension services.

Our ambition is to help bridge the gap between advanced satellite observations and practical agricultural decisions. By making Earth-science information easier to explore and interpret, TerraField Atlas aims to contribute to more informed crop planning, improved environmental awareness, more resilient agricultural practices and better use of scientific data.

The platform also has wider potential for climate adaptation research, environmental monitoring, agricultural development programmes and food-security initiatives.

What technologies and tools were used?

The engineering approach is based on geospatial computing, scientific data processing and modern web application development.

Our selected technology architecture includes:

  • NASA Earth observation: NASA POWER for meteorological information, MODIS vegetation indices for vegetation monitoring, and SMAP for satellite-derived soil-moisture observations.
  • NASA FIRMS: MODIS and VIIRS active-fire observations for potential landscape-monitoring extensions.
  • Frontend: TypeScript, React and Next.js for the interactive application.
  • Geospatial visualization: MapLibre GL for interactive maps and geographic data layers.
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI for data processing, analytical services and application APIs.
  • Scientific computing: GeoPandas, Rasterio, Xarray, NumPy, Pandas and SciPy for geospatial and statistical processing.
  • Database: PostgreSQL and PostGIS for structured records and spatial information.
  • Data visualization: Interactive time-series charts, environmental indicators and geospatial comparisons.

These tools provide the foundation for connecting Earth-observation datasets with spatial analysis and agricultural decision support.

How is the project creative and innovative?

The central innovation is the integration of Earth-observation intelligence with explainable agricultural planning.

Satellite platforms produce enormous quantities of environmental information, but that information is not automatically useful to a farmer deciding what to plant next. TerraField Atlas focuses on translating observations into a practical decision-making workflow.

Its approach connects three complementary capabilities:

  1. Environmental intelligence: understanding what is happening across an agricultural landscape.
  2. Scientific trend analysis: examining how environmental conditions change over time.
  3. Agricultural decision support: comparing possible crop-rotation strategies against available environmental and soil information.

The architecture also creates opportunities to extend the platform into related Earth-observation applications, including environmental trend detection and harmonized MODIS/VIIRS fire monitoring.

What factors did the team consider?

Several important factors influenced the design:

  • Scientific accuracy: Environmental observations must be interpreted according to their actual spatial resolution, temporal coverage and measurement limitations.
  • Data reliability: Missing observations, cloud contamination, quality flags, inconsistent datasets and external API failures must be considered.
  • Local relevance: Agricultural recommendations need to account for regional crops, growing seasons, soil characteristics and farmer priorities.
  • Explainability: Recommendations should expose their underlying evidence, scoring methodology, assumptions and uncertainty.
  • Accessibility: The application should remain understandable and usable by people without specialist remote-sensing or data-science knowledge.
  • Scalability: The architecture should accommodate additional geographical regions, environmental datasets and agricultural use cases.
  • Practical impact: The objective is not simply to visualize data, but to help users explore better-informed agricultural decisions.

TerraField Atlas represents our vision of making space-based science more accessible on the ground: transforming NASA Earth observations into understandable intelligence that can help communities prepare for environmental change and build more resilient agricultural systems.
